races.name: Seamus Byrne Electrical Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Anyway
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for David Budds who has been off 105 days and returns with a mixed recent form string including two pulled-up efforts; visor worn, similar-going form reads 2 wins from 15 starts, and at 8 years old with 164lbs, needs to produce a career-best to be a factor at OR 136.
runners_data.comment: Anyway has run over today's trip and going, and his official mark of 136 gives him solid claims as a leading danger in this field, yet winless in his last five starts and returning after 105 days off, he must prove that freshness rather than rustiness is the result of that lengthy absence.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: Declan Queally's yard is in a 5/11 14-day strike rate and this horse won last time out over 25f on good ground; the sole pace-setter here, fresh off a 6-day turnaround, and the ability to control all fractions on yielding Tramore ground is the defining tactical factor in this race.
runners_data.comment: Rocky's Diamond won last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving him strong claims at the top of the weights on 164 lb; the pulled-up run two starts back is the only blot, but his latest victory makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Thecompanysergeant
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up horse for Gavin Cromwell and Keith Donoghue who finished second last time out over 20f on good; blinkers fitted, and his 2 wins from 15 runs on similar going show he handles conditions, though he needs the pace to quicken late — that may not happen here.
runners_data.comment: Thecompanysergeant won two starts back and was a close second three starts back, showing he arrives in solid heart; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 164 lb the weight burden is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: More Coko
runners_data.note: Mullins's 6-year-old, returning after 131 days off, has raced at much shorter distances (16-17f typically) and steps up in trip here; a natural hold-up horse, his finishing efforts will depend entirely on whether Rocky's Diamond sets a demanding enough gallop to flatten out on the run-in.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 131 days, More Coko does have going experience and a trainer firing at 30% in the past fortnight to recommend him; the concern is that two recent sixths and a fall make his current form hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Joe
runners_data.note: Lightly-raced six-year-old who typically fades in the finish and whose natural role is at the rear of the field; trainer 0/1 in the 14-day window, 10 days since last run, and with limited form data (just two recorded runs) the [STYLE_FIT] tag tempers confidence that he can capitalise even if positioned closer than usual.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and lightly raced, Rodeo Joe has been through a rough patch with three consecutive pull-ups before an unplaced effort ten days ago, yet to win in recent starts, though he returns quickly and the 152 lb burden will need factoring in.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only five runners and no genuine pace rival to push him, Declan Queally's six-year-old should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 2m6f trip on yielding ground at Tramore. Thecompanysergeant, More Coko, and Rodeo Joe are all natural hold-up horses, while Anyway will look to track from a prominent position but is unlikely to force the pace. This creates a scenario where Rocky's Diamond can set an honest but unhurried tempo, potentially controlling the fractions and presenting himself fresh at every fence — a shape that strongly favours a front-runner capable of jumping and staying at their own rhythm rather than deep closers who need a searching gallop to reel them in. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate, and while Rodeo Joe is redistributed to midfield for mapping purposes, its true role is at the rear; the closers here will need a genuine injection of pace in the final half-mile to close on a leader who has controlled his own race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rocky's Diamond Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond is allowed to dictate a measured, uncontested pace from the front and jumps accurately throughout.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond sets the fractions on his own terms, conserving energy through the yielding ground, and has enough left to repel any late challenge from the hold-up brigade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond sets a genuinely strong pace that burns his energy reserves, opening the door for the hold-up horses late.
scenarios.body: Thecompanysergeant and More Coko, operating from the rear, would relish a truly-run race that creates maximum attrition over the final two fences and the run-in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Anyway Tracks and Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Anyway travels powerfully just off Rocky's Diamond's shoulder and the leader fades in the straight.
scenarios.body: With a prominent racing style and form showing competitive runs at this sort of trip, Anyway could exploit any weakness in the leader at the business end of the race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond makes a significant jumping error early, scrambling the race order and forcing a different pace dynamic.
scenarios.body: A mid-race reshuffle on yielding ground at Tramore could compress the field and produce a sprint finish that suits a horse with residual freshness — Thecompanysergeant's recent course form would make him dangerous in that scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Rocky's Diamond's jumping at the early fences — a clean round will entrench his tactical advantage, but any error on yielding ground could collapse the 71% dominant scenario and let the closers back into it.

Monitor the pace at the halfway point; if Rocky's Diamond has set an unusually slow tempo, Anyway may be poised just behind and could pounce before the hold-up horses can wind up, shifting weight from Scenario A to Scenario C.

Thecompanysergeant has blinkers fitted and Donoghue is a seasoned jumps jockey — if the hold-up scenario does materialise, this pairing represents the most credible threat from the rear, especially given two recent finishes of 1st and 2nd.

More Coko's 131-day absence combined with a significant step up in trip (from 16-17f to 2m6f) is a notable query; watch in-running for any sign of distress approaching the final two fences which would confirm he needs this run.

Rodeo Joe has shown a tendency to fade in the finish in limited form, and being pushed into a midfield position out of natural role means his running style creates no meaningful race-shape pressure — watch to see whether Brouder elects to track closer than expected, which would be the only way this horse becomes relevant.

races.name: I.P.R.S. Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Menas Miracle
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling chaser in solid recent form (second at 20f on good) who handles today's trip and going well — strong sim-going record of 12/13 and blinkers likely sharpening focus; has the experience to press Dunany Point from an early stage without over-committing.
runners_data.comment: Bounced back to win two starts back but was pulled up last time out, so reliability is the question mark; she has run over today's distance and going before, and 45 days between runs gives connections time to have her straight, though 168 lb is a stiff burden.

runners_data.name: Mercurial Sea
runners_data.note: Five-year-old still developing, trained by Slevin whose yard is 1/2 in the last fortnight; races prominently and has placed four times without winning, suggesting a reliable finisher who may lack the decisive kick to reel in a well-positioned rival late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but has two runner-up finishes in that sequence, and she has run over today's trip and going before; the weight of 164 lb and a ranking of seventh from seventeen suggest she holds a midfield chance at best.

runners_data.name: Pirate Island
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up performer wearing a tongue-strap and pad, off just 11 days and with a modest recent sim-going record of 8/15 — jumping has been inconsistent and his best Tramore hope relies on a strongly-run race which Dunany Point's pace may not fully supply.
runners_data.comment: Pirate Island has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 98 ranks him fourth of 17, making him a live threat on his best form — yet winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up effort in there, that consistency question is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: My Cullen
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with a remarkable sim-going record of 15/15 and four places from five recent starts; Hanlon's yard is quiet in the last 14 days (0/23) but the horse finds himself perfectly placed stylistically to sit handy and challenge from the second-last.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and shouldering 160 lb with a trainer who has gone 0/21 in the last fortnight, My Cullen faces a stiff ask, though the second last time out hints at some residual ability and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Our Zebo
runners_data.note: Long absence (329 days off) is the dominant factor for this Kelly-trained seven-year-old, though he has three wins and seven places in similar going conditions and was placed twice over today's trip — stamina is not in doubt but race-fitness is a real question after nearly a year off.
runners_data.comment: Our Zebo shaped with promise when third three starts back and a winner two starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going; our rating of 103 makes him the one to beat, though an absence of 329 days is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Thewaybackhome
runners_data.note: Prominent five-year-old from a trainer in form (1/5 in 14 days) who finished second at 2m5f in similar conditions last time; this represents a drop in OR from recent efforts and he looks well handicapped if he can replicate that prominent role on today's slightly shorter trip variant.
runners_data.comment: Thewaybackhome has placed twice in his last three starts — second last time out and third three starts back — but remains winless in recent starts and carries a hefty 159 lb, which may test his resolution here despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Dunany Point
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who will control the pace from the gate — Maxwell's yard is 1/4 in the last fortnight, the horse is lightly weighted at OR 85 and wore a hood previously; on this going and over 2m6f, the question is whether he has enough quality to sustain his advantage rather than simply set up a race for others.
runners_data.comment: Dunany Point showed a glimmer last time out with a third, though a pull-up two starts back clouds his recent profile, and he remains winless in his last five starts; has run over today's going and returns after 23 days, but 155 lb is a stiff ask for a horse ranked tenth of seventeen.

runners_data.name: Not So Serious
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who won over 22f on good ground last time and was a DNF on several starts before that — Slevin in the saddle is a notable positive and the horse, while naturally a hold-up type, is not heavily redistributed and can find a suitable position in a strung-out field over this stiff trip.
runners_data.comment: Returned to winning ways last time out and arrives here 24 days later with experience of today's trip and going, while our rating of 102 marks him as a serious threat — though three pulled-up efforts in recent starts remain the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Corkbeg
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up specialist whose natural race style is at the back of the field, though the volume of true closers in this race means he will likely be pushed closer to the pace than ideal — nine-year-old carrying 154lbs and with no wins from 15 similar-going runs, his chance depends heavily on the race truly getting away from the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 12 of 17 on our ratings, Corkbeg faces a stiff ask carrying 154 lb, though a second in recent starts and experience over today's trip and going give him something to build on just six days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: Bob The Builder
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old flagged as prone to fading in the finish, making his redistribution from hold-up to midfield particularly costly — Rothwell's yard is very active (2/32 in 14 days) but the horse's tendency to empty late rather than stay on strongly limits his prospects in a race run at this distance on yielding ground.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Bob The Builder nonetheless showed a return to form with a third last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before; a career-high 152 lb is the chief concern for a gelding who rates better than his official mark suggests.

runners_data.name: Amburana
runners_data.note: Prominent-style performer carrying just 146lbs after a 23-day break; has placed at 24f in good-ground conditions and ran fourth last time, but trainer Butler (0/2 in 14 days) offers no recent form boost — could creep into it if prominent horses empty but lacks the OR quality to win off merit alone.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 15 of 17 on our figures, Amburana faces a stiff ask here; she does have experience of today's trip and going, and 23 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but her recent string of fourths and worse makes it hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Fr Gilligansvoyge
runners_data.note: A remarkably consistent 13-year-old — one win and five places from recent runs, with a sim-going record of 14/15 — who races naturally at the back of the field; in a race where true closers are crowded out, his experience and reliable jumping give him the best chance of any redistributed hold-up type to still deliver late.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Fr Gilligansvoyge is hard to fancy despite a win three starts back and placed efforts last time out and two starts back; he has experience over today's trip and going, but 145 lb is a stiff ask for a runner rated just 75.

runners_data.name: Set The Tone
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who has won and placed at 22-24f on good ground and showed real promise last year, but his natural hold-up style is compressed by the field shape — wearing a tongue-strap, last ran just 7 days ago, and while the short turnaround from Carr's operation (0/1 in 14 days) is neutral, racing out of position is the key concern.
runners_data.comment: Set The Tone scrambled home a winner two starts back but has since finished sixth, and at 145 lb against 16 rivals our rating ranks her near the foot of the field, making her hard to recommend despite the fitness edge of a run just seven days ago.

runners_data.name: Robin Elite
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish and with a poor recent record (?/P/P/0/P in last five), this hold-up performer is pushed into a midfield position that only adds to his structural disadvantage — at OR 72 and racing without a clear late-race role, he is a significant outsider even in a race that scrambles the order.
runners_data.comment: Robin Elite has pulled up three times in recent starts and is winless in his last five, with a ranking of 16 of 17 on our figures; he carries 142 lb and, while he has run over today's going before, it is very hard to make a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Tropical Image
runners_data.note: An interesting hold-up performer at OR 87, potentially well-handicapped, who has won and placed regularly in similar going (sim record 13/15) — without a named jockey listed he carries a flag around market confidence, but his style and stamina profile make him one of the more dangerous deep closers if the race unfolds with any genuine early tempo.
runners_data.comment: Tropical Image has run over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back shows she retains some ability, but she is winless in her last five starts and a lofty 157 lb is a stern ask for a mare ranked towards the foot of this field.

runners_data.name: U Asking Me
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer at OR 78 whose natural finishing position is the rear of the field — the crowded hold-up division in this race forces him forward, which is where he has historically struggled; the trainer (0/1 in 14 days) offers nothing additional and his two pulls-up from recent runs add to the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — including a pull-up and two deep finishes — U Asking Me faces a stiff task ranked 14 of 17 on our figures, though he has run over today's going before and 28 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Shantou Show
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old hold-up type at OR 95 — the highest-rated horse in the race — who is well-suited in terms of trip and going (sim record 14/15, placed at 26f) but whose last three runs include a pull-up and two mid-pack finishes; if he is fully tuned after 23 days and gets a clear run from his natural position, he is the highest-class threat in the field.
runners_data.comment: Third two starts back shows he retains ability, and he returns 23 days later in good order, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; winless in recent starts, but our figures suggest he holds strong claims under 165 lb.

races.paceDynamic: Dunany Point is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 17 and will stride to the front unchallenged, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m6f of yielding Tramore ground. Behind him, Menas Miracle, Mercurial Sea, My Cullen, and Thewaybackhome will press for prominent positions, creating a compact and competitive early order without burning excessive pace. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate — Corkbeg, Bob The Builder, Fr Gilligansvoyge, Set The Tone, Robin Elite, and U Asking Me are all genuine hold-up horses but several will be forced to race more prominently than they prefer, compromising their ability to produce their natural late run. With one honest front-runner controlling an honest but unforced gallop on yielding ground over this stamina-testing trip, this race shape most strongly favours prominent racers who can travel with cover in second or third, conserve energy through the middle, and pick off the leader from the second-last fence — giving horses like Menas Miracle, Thewaybackhome, and Tropical Image the clearest tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dunany Point Dictates, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point leads at a sustainable clip and prominent challengers track him into the straight with fuel in reserve.
scenarios.body: Dunany Point's uncontested lead on yielding ground sets a rhythm that suits horses who have travelled prominently — they reach the last fence with enough left to wear him down or stride past. Menas Miracle, Thewaybackhome, and My Cullen are ideally drawn in terms of race position and all have the stamina profile for this trip on this ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Runs Them Ragged, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Dunany Point's pace proves more relentless than it appears and the prominent horses overcook it chasing him.
scenarios.body: Dunany Point, suited by forcing tactics and relatively lightly weighted at OR 85, gallops the field into submission on the long Tramore run-in, with the pack failing to close. Horses that sat slightly deeper and conserved — Not So Serious and Tropical Image — finish strongest of all without quite getting to him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalker Finishes Best
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely honest enough to see prominent horses tied up, allowing a resolute midfield traveller to reel them in.
scenarios.body: A horse that sits sixth to eighth with a smooth passage and jumps well throughout finds the prominent pack emptying after the second-last, allowing a strong, stamina-based finish to tell. Tropical Image and Not So Serious — both effective hold-up performers not overly displaced by the race shape — profile best here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles the Order
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, a crowded 17-runner field, or early fallers disrupt the expected pace structure entirely.
scenarios.body: With 17 runners on a track like Tramore, incidents are genuinely possible — fences bypassed, horses impeded, or the pace fragmenting into multiple bunches. Runners with proven jumping reliability and adaptability, such as Fr Gilligansvoyge and Our Zebo, benefit most when the map is thrown into disorder.

watchPoints.text: Dunany Point — if he builds an unchallenged lead of more than four lengths down the back, the race may already be over for the hold-up brigade before the final circuit even begins.

Shantou Show — highest OR (95) in the race and suited by trip and going, but has pulled up twice recently; watch for whether he travels with his usual fluency from an early stage as an indicator of his participation.

Our Zebo — 329 days absent is a significant fitness flag in a stamina race over 2m6f on yielding ground; if he travels sweetly in the early stages he represents live each-way interest, but any sign of struggle before halfway and he can be dismissed.

Crowding risk at the first fence with 17 runners — Tramore's tight, undulating track and a large field makes the opening stages particularly volatile; hold-up horses pushed forward (Corkbeg, Bob The Builder, Fr Gilligansvoyge) are most exposed to interference in these opening strides.

Fr Gilligansvoyge — at 13 years old and with genuine consistent form (14/15 in similar going), watch whether he jumps fluently in the early stages; if he does and gets any kind of run on the final bend, he is capable of finishing closer than his age and race position suggest.

races.name: Majestic Hotel Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Chasing Blues
runners_data.note: A front-runner for De Bromhead who has run on good and soft without winning in hurdling; headgear flagged, 22 days since last run, and facing two rivals with equal pace intentions makes a clean lead very unlikely — likely to race fiercely early and pay for it.

runners_data.name: Fortis Et Liber
runners_data.note: Ricky Doyle partners this Colin Bowe-trained five-year-old on hurdling debut over a trip that looks adequate; the single run shows a place on good ground and prominent style is well-suited to a stop-start pace where holding a handy position could be decisive.

runners_data.name: Jack Spriggins
runners_data.note: 728 days absent is a critical flag — whatever flat form exists is essentially irrelevant on return to hurdling; Kevin Healy partners a horse with scattered placed form on soft that will need to survive the layoff before being judged.

runners_data.name: Jury Foreman
runners_data.note: Runs from OR 94 with a tongue-tie and a poor recent record including a U (unseated), and trainer Paul Nolan is 1/8 in the past 14 days; confirmed front-runner who is likely to push the pace hard but has no wins or places over hurdles to justify confidence in the finish.

runners_data.name: Nothintodowithme
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for Barry Murphy whose sole hurdle run ended in a pull-up on good ground; tongue-tie applied, 80 days off, and a 5lb claiming rider suggests this is a confidence-building run rather than a win bid.

runners_data.name: O'Callaghan Can
runners_data.note: Has placed three times in five hurdle runs including twice over 2m2f at Tramore, showing this track and trip suit him; prominent style with 5lb claimer Alan O'Sullivan aboard, and consistent placed form on good ground makes him a natural fit if the pace sorts out the field.

runners_data.name: Seven Towers
runners_data.note: Keith Donoghue takes over for Gavin Cromwell, who is 3/22 in the past 14 days; four placed efforts from five hurdle runs show consistent competitiveness off genuine gallops, and the step up from 2m to 2m½f on yielding ground should suit his stamina profile.

runners_data.name: World As One
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes rides for the powerful Mullins yard, which is 13/40 in the past 14 days — a strong operational marker; confirmed front-runner with a tongue-tie and a place over 2m4f on soft, and if he can secure a lead without being pressed hard, his class edges above the other pace horses.

runners_data.name: Champ Young
runners_data.note: James Barrett's four-year-old has two runs showing modest form; in reality a hold-up type by style but the density of rear-runners in this field means he is unlikely to get that position — running against his nature tempers any expectation significantly.

runners_data.name: Hashtag Doyen
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old lightly raced over hurdles — just one run — with 117 days off and a 7lb claimer for Mark Fahey, who is 0/7 in the past fortnight; style is uncertain and nothing in the profile suggests a winning threat here.

runners_data.name: Isthatrightkatie
runners_data.note: 390 days since last run is a significant concern for a horse flagged as a fader in finishes; three hurdle runs all resulted in mid-to-rear finishes on good ground, and the combination of lengthy absence and finishing pattern makes this a low-priority runner.

runners_data.name: The Orphan Girl
runners_data.note: Peter Fahey has had 0 winners from 9 runs in 14 days and this six-year-old is flagged as a fader; only back 11 days after her last run and with a headgear flag, the form profile — sole hurdle run finished ninth — gives little encouragement in a competitive maiden.

runners_data.name: Simple Things
runners_data.note: JP Dempsey's four-year-old has placed twice at 2m4f on soft/good-to-soft and the staying profile is genuine; a true hold-up horse pushed toward midfield by field congestion, so will need things to fall right — the style fit discount is real but the stamina credentials are among the better in the field.

races.paceDynamic: World As One, Chasing Blues, and Jury Foreman are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset over 2m½f on yielding ground at Tramore — a track that already tests stamina through its undulating nature. With three horses fighting for the lead, no single pacemaker can dictate comfortably; the pace is likely to be genuine and sustained, burning off one-paced types but creating a test that rewards those who can travel powerfully within the race before asserting. This shape strongly favours prominent-to-midfield runners with genuine stamina and a clean jumping record — horses who can sit just off a hot pace without being pulled wide, then pick off the fading front-runners in the closing stages. Champ Young and Simple Things are true hold-up horses shuffled forward on the map due to field congestion at the rear — Seven Towers, Fortis Et Liber, and O'Callaghan Can are the more natural prominent types who are actually equipped to secure those positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Fries Frontmen
scenarios.trigger: If World As One, Chasing Blues, and Jury Foreman push hard against each other and the pace is unrelenting from the first hurdle, the front three tie each other up and leave the door open for prominent trackers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Seven Towers and O'Callaghan Can have repeatedly placed off honest gallops and Tramore's stamina test suits their profile; the yielding ground ensures the front-runners pay a price for fighting over the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Front-Runner Leads Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three pace horses — most likely World As One under Brian Hayes for Mullins — breaks well and establishes a clear lead before the others settle, dictating at a more controlled but still searching gallop.
scenarios.body: World As One has placed at Grade level over 2m4f on soft ground and the Mullins/Hayes combination adds significant class; from a more settled position in front, the horse's stamina becomes a weapon rather than a liability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Favours Midfielders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the back straight and riders in mid-division find daylight, horses with genuine stamina reserves travelling wide of the scrimmage can challenge.
scenarios.body: Simple Things has placed twice over 2m4f on soft/good-to-soft and, though pushed out of a true hold-up position by field congestion, has the staying profile to capitalise if traffic opens; O'Callaghan Can's course form over 2m4f and 2m2f at Tramore is a live asset here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the front three genuinely go too hard and the field implodes late, freeing up a true hold-up horse to sprint from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Champ Young and Jack Spriggins are the deepest-sitting types but both carry significant concerns — Champ Young is redistributed from a true rear position and Jack Spriggins has not raced in 728 days; a late-run scenario is the least reliable given the hold-up contingent is thinned by redistribution.

watchPoints.text: World As One, Chasing Blues, and Jury Foreman could have a fierce battle for the lead from the outset — watch whether any of the three breaks cleanly enough to dictate, or whether all three race into each other's pockets and set up the race for those behind.

Seven Towers has been placed in four of five hurdle starts and Keith Donoghue is a significant booking — watch his position tracking the pace through the back straight, as any deterioration in the leaders' stride is likely to bring him into contention.

Simple Things and Champ Young are genuine hold-up horses mapped forward due to field congestion — watch whether either can actually drop back to their natural position at the start, as failing to do so would see them racing too prominently for their style.

Jack Spriggins has been off 728 days — watch his jumping in the early stages; any hesitation or error at the first two hurdles would confirm this is a fitness outing and remove him from calculations entirely.

O'Callaghan Can has placed twice at Tramore over this trip — watch whether Alan O'Sullivan settles him in a handy position on the first circuit, as his course form is the strongest track-specific angle in the field and a clean round of jumping could be decisive.

races.name: John Fairbrother Memorial Mares Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Del Boys Diva
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up mare for Shane Crawley who fades in the finish — her two wins at similar going and trip are a positive, but ORs of 0-0 in her last two and a fade flag make her hard to trust off a slow pace that will not generate the late rush she needs.
runners_data.comment: Del Boys Diva arrives in fine nick off back-to-back wins, though the burden of 166 lb is a notable ask, and she has been unplaced in two of her last five starts; she has run over today's trip and going before, so conditions hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Galileo Springs
runners_data.note: Martin Brassil's mare is the lone front-runner here and holds a strong record at this trip (1W, 6P from 11 similar-going runs), but her STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) reflects she may not get a truly uncontested lead with several prominent types pressing from behind — fitness is fine at 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Galileo Springs arrives here in fine trim, winning two starts back and filling the frame last time out, and she has experience of both today's trip and conditions; the weight of 163 lb is the one factor her supporters must account for.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott-trained five-year-old who races from hold-up in headgear; her Curragh and Navan form is limited in scope and sim-going figures (0W/0P from 5 runs) do not inspire, and 11 days between runs with a P on recent form is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Golden Wings has run over today's trip and returns quickly on 11 days' rest, but her recent record gives pause — seventh last time out, and a third four starts back are the brightest notes in a sequence that also includes a pulled-up effort, leaving her winless in her last five starts carrying 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on good and has placed at this trip, but a finishing fade flag and a dire recent run (0-from-14 at this going band in sim figures) combine to suppress confidence; P E Collins's stable at 1/1 T14 is a small sample positive, nothing more.
runners_data.comment: Small Bucks won two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, giving her solid claims here off a 16-day turnaround; the concern is that she has been unplaced on either side of that victory, suggesting some inconsistency to overcome.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson (claimer) partners this mare who holds a compelling recent form profile — 1W, 7P from 15 similar-going runs, placed at this trip twice this season — and her natural prominent style slots her perfectly into the likely race shape behind Galileo Springs.
runners_data.comment: Sea Of Doubt returns in fine fettle just 17 days after her latest outing, with experience of today's trip and going working in her favour; the unseating on her most recent start is a blot, and a bold show under 162 lb looks well within reach.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: Carl Millar (5lb claimer) takes the ride for a trainer with no current 14-day form; at nine years old she is exposed, but her two wins at 16f on good ground and a second at 16f here in the past are relevant — 42 days off is worth noting and she may need it.
runners_data.comment: Tingarran Express showed smart form with a second two starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead; the concern is that nine-week absence, given she was beaten ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Like An Ocean
runners_data.note: Very lightly raced four-year-old (just two career runs) with a win over 16f on good; Adrian Sexton's stable at 0/6 in the 14-day window is a caution, and Harry Sexton (7lb claim) reduces the weight meaningfully — the inexperience at this level is the real question mark.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but managed only seventh last time out, Like An Ocean has experience of both today's trip and going — she steps in carrying 158 lb, which is the key query against her claims here.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: J J Slevin takes the mount for Ms Margaret Mullins in what is one of the most significant jockey bookings in the race; genuinely a front-running/prominent type whose true style has been pushed back to midfield on the map — in a field with this much pace, she may well end up off the bridle earlier than ideal and her STYLE_FIT (0.90) reinforces that concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Rare Times faces a stiff ask under 150 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bravewhenineedtobe
runners_data.note: Returning after 717 days off — that layoff is the dominant factor here regardless of anything else; a natural prominent operator for Margaret Mullins who will be unable to get that position freely given the traffic ahead, and a STYLE_FIT of 0.93 underlines the mismatch between her natural role and the one she'll be asked to fill.
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 717 days makes Bravewhenineedtobe extremely difficult to assess, and she ranks ninth of ten on our figures, so the case against her is stark; she does arrive on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, which are the only crumbs of comfort here.

runners_data.name: Cinnabar Moth
runners_data.note: Liz Doyle's five-year-old is the lowest-rated runner in the field (OR=81) with a string of 5-9 finishes in recent form on good ground; she carries a finishing fade flag and her true hold-up style is already crowded in the mapping — this is a race where her profile finds very little comfort.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Cinnabar Moth faces a stiff ask at 142 lb, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 22-day break.

races.paceDynamic: Galileo Springs is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival likely to push her early, she shapes to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop on yielding ground over 2m½f at Tramore. Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, and Like An Ocean are all prominent-style horses who will seek to track closely, meaning a small lead group forms but without any combustion — this is a controlled rather than contested tempo. The redistribution flags are significant: Rare Times and Bravewhenineedtobe are natural prominent types who will be squeezed back from their preferred berths, and Cinnabar Moth — a hold-up mare — is also displaced; none of the three is likely to secure their natural tactical position. A moderate, metronomic pace on yielding ground over this trip at Tramore is a classically unhelpful shape for true hold-up horses, instead favouring horses that can travel prominently and produce a sustained effort from three out rather than a late sprint — the patient-prominent or stalking profile is the one to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galileo Springs Controls, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Galileo Springs sets an uncontested moderate fractions and the race is won from the tracking positions.
scenarios.body: Galileo Springs dictates from the front, Sea Of Doubt and Tingarran Express shadow her into the straight, and the winner emerges from that small lead group as stamina counts on the yielding ground; hold-up horses simply cannot generate enough pace late to bridge a large gap off a slow tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Prominent Types Tested
scenarios.trigger: If the moderate early pace suddenly increases from three out and the stalking group is put to the test sooner than expected.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Doubt's consistent form against competitive fields and her strong placed record over similar trips at this level makes her ideally suited if the tempo lifts mid-race, as she has the class and fitness to respond; Tingarran Express, a past winner at this trip on good ground, also handles a test of stamina well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Galileo Springs is simply allowed to control the race so completely that no rival can close her down on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 discounting her chance under pressure, this scenario demands Galileo Springs reproduce her best (her OR=102 win form is there) and the yielding conditions help neutralise the closing kick of hold-up rivals; this outcome is plausible but depends on nothing going wrong and the stalkers underperforming.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically, creating a falsely run race that compresses the field and allows the rear-rankers to swoop.
scenarios.body: Del Boys Diva and Golden Wings are the only genuine hold-up runners in their natural position, but both carry finishing fade concerns and their sim-going figures are modest; Bravewhenineedtobe and Cinnabar Moth, though redistributed from their true prominent roles, would need to be ridden entirely against type to play a part here — this is the least likely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sea Of Doubt can track Galileo Springs in the first three from early — if she locks onto the front-runner's girth before the second last, she becomes the most dangerous horse in the race given her prominent style, consistent placed record, and competent claimer booking.

Galileo Springs's STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) means she may be challenged off her controlled front-running game if Sea Of Doubt, Tingarran Express, or Like An Ocean crowd her early — any pressure would undermine her dominant scenario probability.

Bravewhenineedtobe's 717-day absence is exceptional and must be respected; even if Margaret Mullins has her ready, this mare will not be straightforward tactically and should be treated as a significant unknown regardless of her ability on fresher form.

Like An Ocean (4yo, two career runs, 7lb claim) is a wild card — unexposed mares with a single win can outrun their odds in this type of race, and if the yard has prepared her well she could be a big price surprise from the prominent group.

The going for this race is reported Yielding by the racecourse despite the official card saying Good To Soft — this is relevant for any runner with a proven preference for cut, and the discrepancy should be factored into reading finishing positions.

races.name: Walsh Butler Electrical Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Banphrionsa Alainn
runners_data.note: Lightly-exposed with a T14 return of 0/3, this mare is a genuine hold-up type shifted into a midfield slot only because rear positions are severely overcrowded; the 13-day turnaround is fine but the fade-in-finish flag and lack of any win or placing make appeal thin.

runners_data.name: Fervida
runners_data.note: Modest OR of 78 and a form string littered with pulled-up and unseated codes on good and soft ground; carries the hold-up fade warning and though her natural rear-racing style suits a truly-run race, her record offers little reason to upgrade her.

runners_data.name: Hello Below
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed pace-setter, which gives her a unique positional advantage in this field; won and placed at up to 22f on good ground, the yielding surface is untested but her ability to control tempo is the defining structural feature of this race.

runners_data.name: Hunskelper
runners_data.note: Gordon — sorry, Cian Collins-trained five-year-old returning after a 90-day break with a T14 strike of 1/15; a true hold-up mare whose best effort of 6th came at 16f, stepping up to 21f on yielding is an unproven combination, and the layoff adds doubt.

runners_data.name: Mila Ballerina
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and showed improvement when fifth over 18f on good ground last time; a genuine hold-up type but with the visor possibly sharpening her early deployment, she could sit closer than usual and that would suit the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Nancy Wheeler
runners_data.note: Darragh O'Keeffe takes the ride for Stuart Curling, who is 0/6 in the past fortnight; Nancy has finished no higher than 11th in three starts and all three came on going faster than today's yielding, so ground improvement is theoretically possible.

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: Has finished 12th and 15th in two attempts on good ground, both at 17f — stepping up in trip to 21f is the logical try, but Ian Power picks up a mare whose trainer is 0/4 in 14 days and whose record gives little to work with.

runners_data.name: Quiet In Bresil
runners_data.note: Holds a fair bit of experience across 22f on good ground and a solid fifth of seven over 16f; a genuine hold-up type who is mapped to the midfield cluster due to overcrowding at the rear, and the 77-day absence after a tongue-tie run last time warrants watching.

runners_data.name: Road To The Sea
runners_data.note: Fell last time out, which is a jumping concern on a track as demanding as Tramore; one of the redistributed hold-up types carried forward into midfield on the map, and with the lowest finishing positions across five runs, confidence is hard to find.

runners_data.name: Room For One More
runners_data.note: W P Mullins entry with a T14 strike of 13/40, which is the standout training statistic in this race; only fourth outing in public and racing here on the back of four days' rest, the Mullins production line makes her interesting even if her form figures read 6-9-0.

runners_data.name: Treacys Ella
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just two runs showing a fifth and an eighth, both on good ground; style is recorded as unknown which suggests genuine tactical flexibility, and Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim helps with the 161lb burden — Declan Queally is 5/11 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Gratitudeforgrace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old with a T14 figure of 4/43 — Sam Ewing rides and the form shows a 7th and a 12th on good ground; this mare's hold-up tendency means she has been squeezed into the midfield mapping by sheer weight of numbers, and her raw form does not yet justify high expectations.

runners_data.name: I'm Gold
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie, is trained by Olivia Hegarty (0/0 in 14 days), and has finished 13th and 14th in two runs on good ground; a true rear-runner compressed into the midfield picture by field composition, her form figures are the bluntest in the field.

runners_data.name: Kenny's Jewel
runners_data.note: Ridden by J J Slevin, the most high-profile jockey booking for a mid-range hold-up type; wears a hood, has a 6th to her name over 17f and was pulled up on soft previously — the hood and Slevin's ability to place her better than her natural position deserve respect.

runners_data.name: Thedreamistilalive
runners_data.note: Wears a tongue-tie and has finished 15th and 9th in two runs for Donncha Duggan who is 1/6 in 14 days; a 13-day turnaround is fine but the hold-up fade flag and a finishing record anchored at the back of fields makes this a tough race for her to threaten.

runners_data.name: Lady Aquarelle
runners_data.note: Most experienced runner in the field with five career starts, wears tongue and blinkers, and her best effort is a 7th over 22f on soft — ground today is analogous; this hold-up mare is displaced into the midfield cluster on the map, and her prior soft-ground seventh at least suggests stamina on give.

races.paceDynamic: Hello Below is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-mare field and looks set to dictate from the front at a sustainable, uncontested gallop over 2m5f on yielding ground at Tramore — a track that already places a premium on jumping fluency and stamina. With no other genuine lead horse to challenge her, she can control tempo and conserve energy through the middle stages, which sets up a race that should be decided by finishing resolution rather than raw pace. The yielding surface and extended trip will test the staying power of hold-up runners, and with the majority of the field being true closers competing for the same ground in the straight, scrimmaging risks are high late on. This shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the pace who can travel smoothly into contention without needing a clear run from deep; pure hold-up profiles face a traffic-heavy, ground-dependent ask. Several runners listed here — including I'm Gold, Hunskelper, Gratitudeforgrace, Kenny's Jewel, Road To The Sea, and Lady Aquarelle — are genuine hold-up types compressed into a midfield mapping because the field is overwhelmingly rear-ward in tendency, and it is Hello Below alone who is most likely to secure her natural position at the head of affairs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hello Below Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Below gets a clean break and sets a measured, uncontested pace from the front on the yielding ground.
scenarios.body: Hello Below dictates a controlled tempo with no rival willing or able to press her, conserving energy for the final climb; horses racing in her slipstream — within two to three lengths — will be ideally placed to pounce if she tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners ignore their hold-up tendencies and chase Hello Below into a stronger gallop, cranking up the pace.
scenarios.body: A more truly-run race on the yielding surface stretches the field and produces a stamina test in the final half-mile; horses with proven staying form who have raced handily before will be rewarded as the front pair empty.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up The Pieces
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Below's early pace proves deceptively quick on the yielding surface and she fades before the last, opening a gap for closers.
scenarios.body: A collapsing leader can pull the field into a sprint-from-midfield scenario, and the horse with the best stride in the conditions and a clear run through a congested chasing pack will benefit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos And Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the large field produces crowding, jumping errors, and a faltering early pace that turns the finish into a lottery.
scenarios.body: Multiple runners lose their rhythm through interference over the hurdles or a muddling gallop, and only the best-jumping, most-settled mare gets home cleanly; tactical chaos on a yielding Tramore track can throw up a surprising result.

watchPoints.text: Hello Below's ability to maintain fluency over every hurdle is critical — if she makes a significant error at any stage on the yielding surface, her positional advantage evaporates and the entire race dynamic changes.

With at least six genuine hold-up mares all trying to find cover in the early stages, crowding on the first bend and approaching the early hurdles is a real risk — watch for traffic incidents that could shuffle the race before the pace even settles.

Room For One More's four-day turnaround and the W P Mullins booking for a lightly-raced five-year-old warrants close observation in the parade ring — if she travels strongly it is worth noting as the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 13/40 is elite.

Kenny's Jewel with J J Slevin aboard is a combination whose jockey quality exceeds the typical profile for this grade — watch whether Slevin positions her closer than her natural style would suggest, which could signal confidence from connections.

The yielding ground, confirmed for this 7:25 slot by the going report, is softer than most of this field have encountered — any mare showing signs of laboured movement or breathing through the middle stages should be noted as a potential early dropout in a field of 16.

races.name: Comeragh Veterinary Kilmackthomas Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Trainer Declan Queally and jockey partnership is tight (T14: 5/11), last won at 22f on good, handles this trip and going well (sim-going 1W2P), and as a genuine hold-up type needs a strong pace to produce his best finishing effort from off the bridle.
runners_data.comment: Mighty Berkshire arrives here on the back of a win, winning last time out and returning fit after just 16 days, with experience of today's trip and conditions working in his favour; the hefty 167 lb burden is the one factor connections will be hoping doesn't blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Ryan's Son
runners_data.note: Has a win and a second at 16f on good ground but is stepping up significantly in trip here; the fade-in-finish flag is a real concern over 2m5f on a gruelling track, and nothing in his recent form suggests he stays this distance.
runners_data.comment: Ryan's Son won four starts back and arrives here fresh on 35-day absence, with going experience in his favour carrying 166 lb; the worry is two consecutive unplaced efforts heading into this.

runners_data.name: Jacko Star
runners_data.note: 191 days off the track is a significant fitness doubt in a competitive handicap; his five most recent runs all produced placed or beaten efforts at 16-19f, and the step up to 2m5f on yielding ground for a horse returning from six months off looks a tall order.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 191-day absence, Jacko Star faces an obvious fitness query, though he has run over today's going before and a string of fourth-place finishes suggests he is competitive without quite finding the extra gear to win.

runners_data.name: Latopix
runners_data.note: The race's lone confirmed front-runner, trained by Henry De Bromhead and ridden by Darragh O'Keeffe; has placed twice in his last two at 20-22f on good ground, and an uncontested lead over this stamina trip on yielding going plays to his strengths.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Latopix has been placed three times recently but ranks ninth of twelve on our figures and carries a hefty 161 lb, making her hard to fancy; she does have experience of today's distance and going, however.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Fit from a run just 12 days ago, has an excellent record at 24-26f trips on good ground (2W6P from 15 sim-going runs), and his prominent style makes him Latopix's most likely pressurer without having to do it head-to-head.
runners_data.comment: Tullyveery Lad unseated last time out, but a second two starts back shows he retains ability, and returning after just 12 days he arrives fit with experience over today's distance and going; yet to win in recent starts, though our rating of 113 makes him of clear interest under 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Good World
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with a win at 20f on heavy and consistent placing form, but his true running style is hold-up, which is discounted here because he is mapped to midfield out of role; at OR 103, the class is there if he can secure a workable position.
runners_data.comment: Good World won three starts back but has since pulled up and finished unplaced, making his recent form patchy at best; he has run over today's distance and going, and 68 days off at least brings freshness, though 159 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Tolka Row
runners_data.note: Recent winner at 22f on good ground (last run 31 days ago), handles this trip and similar going well (1W2P from 5 sim-going runs), and with a hold-up style that is genuinely suited to a pace-controlled race he looks one of the best-placed closers in the field.
runners_data.comment: Tolka Row arrives on the back of a win last time out and has distance and going experience to call on, with our rating of 108 underlining his strong claims here; the pulled-up effort two starts back is the one risk his supporters must forgive.

runners_data.name: Boston Beach
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner (T14: 4/43) but the fade-in-finish flag is a concern and his best form is at 16-18f — stepping into 2m5f territory on yielding ground for a horse that has finished outside the first three in four of his last five looks problematic; redistributed into midfield because he cannot get his natural hold-up berth in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Boston Beach faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 31-day break carrying 156 lb.

runners_data.name: Hillstar Blues
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with a win at 16f on soft, but 92 days off the track and the fade-in-finish flag raises stamina doubts at 2m5f; as one of several hold-up types displaced into midfield, his chances are structurally undermined by the race shape.
runners_data.comment: Hillstar Blues showed he can win in recent starts, but four subsequent outings have yielded nothing, and 92 days off adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and 150 lb is a stiff burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Diamond Secret
runners_data.note: Ran just yesterday (1 day ago), which is a significant physical concern for any horse regardless of form; his record shows no wins and consistent mid-to-tail finishes, and being a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield adds a further tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Diamond Secret has run over today's trip and going but arrives just a day after finishing unplaced last time out, and is winless in his last five starts — the 149 lb burden does little to help his cause.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Paradise
runners_data.note: Paul Nolan runner with a placing at 24f on good ground, but no wins and no places from 6 similar-going runs; blinkers on and mapped out of natural hold-up position — not straightforward to land even if conditions improve.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts — including a pull-up two outings back — Moonlight Paradise is hard to fancy ranked 11 of 12 on our figures, though she has distance and going experience to call on and 22 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Ray Gun
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a poor recent record (P, 9 in last two), limited sim-going experience (0W0P from 6 runs), and tongue-tie applied; true hold-up style pushed into midfield means he faces a difficult positional task in a race he has few obvious grounds to win.
runners_data.comment: Ray Gun has pulled up twice in his last five starts and is yet to win in that spell, ranking bottom of this field on our figures; the experience over today's trip and going, plus a return after 29 days, offer slim consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Latopix is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him, Darragh O'Keeffe can dictate a controlled, measured gallop from the front over 2m5f on yielding ground at Tramore. The pace will be honest but not injurious — Latopix has placed twice recently at similar distances on good ground and will settle into a rhythm that suits his own stamina profile. Tullyveery Lad is the most likely prominent tracker given his consistent placement record over staying trips, while Good World, Boston Beach, Hillstar Blues, Diamond Secret, Moonlight Paradise and Ray Gun are all genuine hold-up types who have been mapped to midfield because the field contains far more closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — of these, Good World and Tolka Row are the most likely to secure a realistic early position. A controlled front-runner dictating a steady, sustainable pace over a stamina trip on soft-leaning ground is a significant advantage, and this race shape firmly favours hold-up horses with proven finishing power over staying distances who can come from just off the pace — not those forced wide and deep at the back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Latopix Dictates, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Latopix bowls along unchallenged and the pace is steady enough that hold-up horses with genuine stamina close powerfully in the final two flights.
scenarios.body: Latopix controls the tempo and the race becomes a true test of stamina on yielding ground, favouring horses who travel well off the pace and pick up late over the 2m5f trip; hold-up types with good records at this sort of distance and going will be eating into the leader's advantage from two out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Latopix sets is genuinely slow and the midfield/hold-up horses are caught flat-footed or fail to get a clear run through the crowded closing stages.
scenarios.body: Latopix, allowed a soft lead throughout and never seriously challenged, conserves enough energy to repel challengers from the last hurdle home; his recent form of two consecutive placed efforts at similar distances underlines his ability to last home in this style.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse settled just behind Latopix tracks him throughout and produces a decisive jump at the last to collar the leader on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Tullyveery Lad, with a solid record of placing at this trip on good ground and fit from a run 12 days ago, is ideally placed to travel in Latopix's slipstream and challenge once the pace lifts from three out; his consistency over staying trips makes him the natural danger from this position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Overwhelm Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the back straight causing a scramble and multiple hold-up horses manage to get into contention simultaneously, creating a messy finish.
scenarios.body: With so many true hold-up types redistributed into midfield and racing out of their natural role, a chaotic finish is possible but relies on unlikely positioning for most closers; Tolka Row and Mighty Berkshire — the two most organised hold-up types with genuine good-ground stamina form — would benefit most from the resulting scramble.

watchPoints.text: Latopix (front-runner) is uncontested in the lead — watch whether Darragh O'Keeffe deliberately slows the pace from the third-last, which would dramatically reduce the closing window for hold-up horses and make him very hard to peg back.
Tullyveery Lad ran just 12 days ago and is asked to quicken from prominent off a busy schedule — watch for any signs of flat-to-the-boards jumping from the back of the last as fatigue sets in.
Diamond Secret ran yesterday and any sign of a sluggish jump or lack of early pace should be treated as a serious fitness flag, making it one to oppose sharply regardless of odds.

Ryan's Son carries a fade-in-finish flag and has no form beyond 20f — watch whether Eoghan Finegan (5) drops him in early to conserve energy, which would be the only way to give the horse a realistic chance at this trip.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Good World, Boston Beach, Hillstar Blues, Moonlight Paradise, Ray Gun) will all be seeking the same ground from the third-last — watch for traffic congestion on the turn for home that could cost any one of them their chance at a critical moment.

races.name: Clem Jacob Hire Flat Race

runners_data.name: Cloneen To The Max
runners_data.note: Experienced hold-up performer with solid Good-ground profile (4/5 sim-going runs), but a fader in finishes and forced into a midfield role in this configuration, which blunts his natural patient style; the 7lb claimer Mr A J Browne adds further uncertainty.|
runners_data.comment: Cloneen To The Max shaped with promise when third four starts back, and returns here on a quick 11-day turnaround with conditions to suit, making him a live threat at the weights; the concern is that he has been winless in recent starts, with a pulled up and an unplaced run also on his recent card.

runners_data.name: Moonhall Lad
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with an entirely unknown running style and lightly raced flag; trainer Alan McIntyre has sent one from three in the 14-day window, and absence of form figures makes assessment near-impossible without market signals.|

runners_data.name: Tale Of Intrigue
runners_data.note: Progressive chaser with an outstanding 5/5 compatibility on Good ground and a steady climb through the form figures (14-10-3-4-5); the 7lb claimer rides but the improving profile over this trip and going makes it the most interesting tracker in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Third three starts back, and returning on a quick 11-day turnaround having run over today's going, Tale Of Intrigue shapes as a genuine danger carrying 168 lb, though he remains winless in recent starts and that weight could blunt his challenge late on.

runners_data.name: Call My Name
runners_data.note: Four-year-old debutant or returner with no form figures available; trainer Andrew Slattery's 3/30 14-day strike rate is modest but the unknown profile means it must be respected if market support arrives.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to plenty of improvement on debut, Call My Name carries 165 lb and, with no public form to pick over, remains a fascinating unknown who could make an immediate impact yet to score.

runners_data.name: Charles Kickham
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse by inclination, wearing headgear, but pushed into a midfield map position by the weight of hold-up types in this field; beaten eight lengths on Good ground recently and without a win or place in three runs, the style compromise compounds limited recent form.|
runners_data.comment: Charles Kickham has run over today's trip and going, returns fit on a quick ten-day turnaround, and an 89 rating ranking him second of seven makes him a leading threat; the risk is that he has been winless in his last three starts, with a sixth last time out giving pause.

runners_data.name: Mountain Sky
runners_data.note: The race's only genuine front-runner who should lead throughout on Good ground, a surface on which he has run twice with a win-adjacent profile (two seconds); trainer Gerard O'Leary has a 1/12 14-day record but the tactical advantage here is significant.|
runners_data.comment: Mountain Sky has been a model of consistency, finishing second in each of his last two starts, and he returns on a quick ten-day turnaround with experience over today's trip; winless in recent starts, but as the top-rated runner here, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Long'way
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins runner with an exceptional 13/40 14-day trainer strike rate, making it the most powerfully-backed dark horse in the field by stable form alone; unknown style means it could surface anywhere in the race, and market moves pre-race are essential viewing.|
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Long'way heads straight into the unknown, though her trainer is in red-hot form, landing 14 from 47 over the last 14 days, and she carries 161 lb into the contest.

runners_data.name: No Pass Port
runners_data.note: Single run to date produced a ninth on Good ground, the only piece of evidence available; John Joseph Hanlon's 0/23 14-day record is a stark negative, and a fading-in-finish flag makes this the least likely beneficiary of any race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked fifth of seven on our figures, No Pass Port faces a stiff ask here — a ninth last time out does little to inspire confidence, and her trainer is without a strike in 21 attempts over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Mountain Sky is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other genuine pace-setter to challenge, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset over this 2m½f trip on Good ground at Tramore. The field carries more hold-up horses than the rear of the map can accommodate — Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham are natural come-from-behind types who will be forced to race in closer order than ideal, diluting their threat. With Mountain Sky able to set his own fractions uncontested, the race is likely to develop into a test of stamina from the home turn rather than a sprint, as the leader controls the tempo throughout. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and the confirmed front-runner himself, as horses forced to wait for a late run will find limited room to pick off a well-judged leader that has never been asked to go faster than comfortable.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mountain Sky Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Mountain Sky goes to the front immediately and controls a measured, unchallenged gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Mountain Sky sets a comfortable tempo, idles his rivals into submission, and kicks clear from the home turn before stamina tests become critical; his two recent runner-up efforts at this trip suggest he finds his level right here. Prominent horses with the pace to track him closely are best placed, while redistributed hold-up types never get into a winning position arriving too late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mountain Sky's lead is tracked closely by a prominent racer who times a challenge perfectly from two out.
scenarios.body: Mountain Sky sets the race up but is picked off late by a horse that has sat just behind the pace and travels with more ease into the straight; Tale Of Intrigue's improving form over Good ground and 5/5 going compatibility makes it the obvious candidate to exploit this shape. The winner in this scenario is a patient tracker who delivers at the business end without needing a prolonged sprint.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Talent Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly-raced, unknown-style runners — Long'way or Call My Name — proves significantly superior in class or raw ability.
scenarios.body: W P Mullins's Long'way carries the most significant stable ammunition in the field with a 13/40 14-day trainer strike rate, and an unraced profile means the market will reveal plenty; superior ability can overcome any tactical disadvantage. Call My Name, trained by Andrew Slattery who has been in excellent form, cannot be entirely dismissed if debut or return form is sharp.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and exhausted front-runners leave the door open for hold-up horses to come through late.
scenarios.body: Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham are genuine hold-up types forced to race in unnatural midfield positions, severely compromising their ability to deliver a sustained late run; this scenario requires both a faster-than-expected early pace and a genuine stamina collapse, neither of which is set up by the race shape. No Pass Port's single run form of ninth makes this scenario extremely thin without additional evidence.

watchPoints.text: Watch Mountain Sky in the early stages — if he meets zero pressure and establishes a clear lead by the first turn, the race is likely already being run to his strengths and he becomes very difficult to peg back.

Long'way (W P Mullins, 13/40 trainer strike rate) is a significant unknown — monitor its opening price movement closely, as any market support from this yard deserves serious attention in a field where form is otherwise limited.

Cloneen To The Max and Charles Kickham are both natural hold-up horses forced forward by the race shape; if either appears to be fighting for position early rather than settling, their chance is likely gone before halfway.

The going report shows all earlier races at Tramore ran on Yielding, with only this 8:25 race officially listed as Good — watch whether the ground description translates to a meaningfully faster surface that could stretch the stamina of hold-up types arriving late.

Tale Of Intrigue's jockey Mr T A Halford claims 7lbs, which is an unusual combination for a horse showing consistent improvement — check whether the trainer's use of the claimer here signals confidence or caution before assessing the price.|
